summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for acute chest pain associated with dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and diaphoresis. The pain did not respond to nitroglycerin but resolved with morphine. Initial evaluation showed hypotension, EKG changes including T-wave inversions, and a new left lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray concerning for pneumonia, though the patient remained afebrile without cough or leukocytosis. Cardiac biomarkers showed minimal troponin elevation without significant rise, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. A central line was placed for access after peripheral IV failure. The patient developed left hand pain with coolness and weak pulses, likely related to vascular insufficiency from his dialysis fistula; vascular surgery follow-up was recommended. He remained stable, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue medications, and follow up with cardiology and vascular surgery.
